neighbours.label: 'the' after a location verb in cell biology ('located in the', 'found in the'), predicting a cellular compartment; weaker for 'in the soil/slot'
fire: The enzymes of glycolysis are found in the cytoplasm of every cell.
Most of the cell's DNA is stored in the nucleus, wrapped around histones.
These pumps are embedded in the inner membrane of the mitochondria.
Proteins destined for export are folded in the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum.
Chlorophyll is located in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast.
Calcium ions are released from stores inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
The electron transport chain sits in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Digestive enzymes are kept in the lysosome until they are needed.
quiet: The enzymes of glycolysis were described by German chemists long ago.
Most of the cell's DNA was mapped by large teams of researchers.
These pumps use energy from ATP to move ions against a gradient.
Proteins destined for export carry a short signal at one end.
Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
Calcium ions trigger muscle contraction when they bind troponin.
The electron transport chain was worked out over several decades.
Digestive enzymes break down fats, sugars and proteins.
